title: Node.js
summary: A typical Node.js backend job: receive an HTTP request, validate it, check who the user is, read or write a database, return JSON, and keep it running safely in production.

skip.instead: fs/promises + async/await; read callbacks only in legacy code
ES modules ("type": "module" in package.json); know require() well enough to read old code

skip.item: ts-node or a build step just to run TypeScript
skip.instead: Node.js runs .ts files directly (type stripping, stable since v24.12); keep tsc --noEmit for type checks

skip.item: request (deprecated) and axios for simple calls
skip.instead: Built-in fetch; axios is still common in existing code, so learn to read it
Express 5 sends rejected promises from async routes to your error handler (Express 5 migration guide)

skip.item: libuv internals, cluster, worker threads, C++ addons
skip.instead: Learn when a job needs them; rare in API work

skip.item: Framework hopping (NestJS, Fastify, Hono, Koa) in these 8 weeks
skip.instead: Master Express first; the ideas transfer. NestJS is a good next step if your target companies use it

modules.title: Async JavaScript and how Node.js runs it
modules.goal: Write async code without guessing, and know what Node.js does for you before any framework hides it.
learn: Promises, async/await, try/catch, Promise.all / Promise.allSettled
The event loop: call stack, microtasks vs. timers, and why one slow synchronous loop freezes every user's request
ES modules, npm init, npm run scripts, dependencies vs. devDependencies, semver ranges, package-lock.json, npx

build.title: Practice tasks
checklist: Install Node.js 24 LTS with a version manager (nvm, or fnm on Windows)
Fetch data from a public API with built-in fetch; run 3 requests in parallel with Promise.all; handle one failing request cleanly
Predict the print order of setTimeout, setImmediate, Promise.then and process.nextTick — then run it and explain any surprise

modules.title: Core modules
modules.goal: Write async code without guessing, and know what Node.js does for you before any framework hides it.
learn: node:fs/promises, node:path, process (argv, env, exit codes), node:events (EventEmitter)
Streams and pipeline(): process a 1 GB file without loading it into memory
The raw node:http module — once, so you know what Express abstracts

build.title: Gate project: CLI file tool
checklist: Build a raw node:http server with two JSON routes and a 404

doneWhen: A csv-to-json command that streams a large CSV, transforms each row, writes JSON, takes flags via util.parseArgs, and exits with code 1 on bad input. Push it to GitHub with a README.

modules.title: REST APIs with Express 5
modules.goal: Build the thing most Node.js developers build every day — a validated REST API on a real database.
learn: HTTP: methods, status codes (200, 201, 204, 400, 401, 403, 404, 409, 500), headers, path vs. query params
REST design: plural nouns (/notes/:id), pagination, filtering, consistent error shape
Express 5: Router, middleware order, express.json(), async handlers, error middleware (err, req, res, next), a 404 handler
Validation with Zod: parse req.body and req.query, return 400 with field-level errors
Structure: routes → controllers → services, so database code never lives in a route

build.title: Practice tasks
checklist: Build an in-memory "notes" API: list (paginated), get, create, update (PATCH), delete
Add Zod validation and one central error handler returning { error: { code, message } }
Call every endpoint from an HTTP client (Postman, Bruno or VS Code REST Client) and save the collection in the repo

modules.title: PostgreSQL + an ORM
modules.goal: Build the thing most Node.js developers build every day — a validated REST API on a real database.
learn: SQL: SELECT, WHERE, ORDER BY, LIMIT, JOINs, GROUP BY, INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE, primary and foreign keys, indexes, transactions
Parameterised queries with the pg driver — and why building SQL from strings means SQL injection
Prisma ORM: schema, migrations, relations, CRUD, select/include, transactions; spot and fix N+1 queries

build.title: Gate project: CRUD API
checklist: Finish all SQLBolt lessons
Write three raw queries with pg using $1 placeholders

doneWhen: Move the notes API onto PostgreSQL with Prisma — users and notes (one-to-many), tags (many-to-many), committed migrations, pagination, validation, correct 404 and 409 responses

modules.title: Authentication and security
modules.goal: Turn a working API into one a team would merge — users, permissions, tests and logs.
learn: Password hashing with Argon2id (OWASP's first choice) or bcrypt; never store plain or reversible passwords
JWT: a short-lived access token plus a refresh token in an httpOnly cookie, checked by middleware on every request
Sessions vs. JWT: server sessions are simpler for a single app; JWTs suit separate front-ends and services
Authorisation: roles (user, admin) and ownership checks — broken access control is #1 in the OWASP Top 10
Hardening: Helmet headers, a CORS allow-list, rate limiting on login, secrets only in env vars, npm audit

build.title: Practice tasks
checklist: Add register, login, refresh and logout to the notes API
Write requireAuth and requireRole('admin') middleware; a user can edit only their own notes
Add Helmet, CORS and a login rate limit
Use the OWASP Node.js cheat sheet as a checklist against your code

modules.title: Testing, logging and TypeScript
modules.goal: Turn a working API into one a team would merge — users, permissions, tests and logs.
learn: API tests that hit real endpoints against a test database give the most value; unit-test services with real logic; mock only outside services
Vitest (or the built-in node:test) with Supertest
Structured logging with pino: log levels, a request ID per request, never log passwords or tokens
Process safety: unhandledRejection handling and graceful shutdown on SIGTERM
TypeScript: types, interfaces, unions, basic generics, strict mode, typing Express handlers, z.infer to reuse Zod schemas as types

build.title: Gate project: secured API
checklist: Write API tests for every notes endpoint, including the 401, 403 and 404 paths
Add pino request logging
Convert the project to TypeScript with strict: true; run it with Node's built-in type stripping, and add tsc --noEmit to npm test (set erasableSyntaxOnly in tsconfig, so skip enum and namespace)

doneWhen: Auth, roles and a test suite that passes with one command

modules.title: Caching and background jobs
modules.goal: Make it fast, move slow work off the request path, and put it on the internet.
learn: Cache-aside with Redis: check the cache, fall back to the database, store with a TTL, invalidate on writes
What not to cache: per-user secrets, and queries that are already fast
Queues with BullMQ: producers, workers, retries with backoff, delayed jobs, failed-job handling
Keep the event loop free: emails, PDFs and image work belong in a worker, not in the request
Read a query plan with EXPLAIN ANALYZE and fix it with an index

build.title: Practice tasks
checklist: Cache the capstone's public listing endpoint; measure before and after with autocannon
Send confirmation emails from a BullMQ worker (use a test inbox such as Ethereal, not real addresses)
Find your slowest query, add an index, and record the difference

modules.title: Docker, CI/CD and deployment
modules.goal: Make it fast, move slow work off the request path, and put it on the internet.
learn: A production Dockerfile: multi-stage build, npm ci --omit=dev, non-root user, .dockerignore
Docker Compose: API + PostgreSQL + Redis from one command
Config the twelve-factor way: everything from env vars, a /health endpoint, graceful shutdown
CI with GitHub Actions: install → lint → type-check → test on every pull request
Deploy: a container host (Render, Railway or Fly.io) or a small VPS, with managed PostgreSQL (Neon or Supabase); free tiers change often, so check each before you pick

build.title: Gate project: capstone is live
checklist: Dockerise the capstone; docker compose up starts the whole stack
Add a GitHub Actions workflow that runs the tests against a PostgreSQL service container

doneWhen: Deploy it and put the public URL at the top of the README

items: express-async-handler or try/catch in every route → Plain async handlers. Thrown errors reach your error middleware

capstone.title: TicketHub
capstone.summary: An event-booking API that never sells the same seat twice: holds, a payment webhook, a worker, caching and a 50-request concurrency test.
